first.rationale: Two of the three current problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are directly addressable, and the inherited record points at onboarding/signup friction as the highest-leverage lever for self-serve accounts (memory_86, memory_31), with activation messaging as a close second (memory_91). Promotional pricing is the emotionally obvious answer to the competitor's entry pricing, but its supporting memory (memory_73) carries an explicit caveat: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, so the reported acquisition and revenue lift may be an artifact rather than a real effect. Discount-led acquisition also poses the clearest downstream risk to the primary objective: it can buy volume of price-sensitive accounts while degrading the quality and durability of revenue, which is precisely what 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' excludes. That is why I spend one verification pull on memory_73 - not because I intend to run it, but because if the source record turns out to be clean and the lift is real and durable, the competitive pressure would justify reopening the choice. The second pull goes to memory_86 because it is the direct basis for my intended action and it reports proxy outcomes (completion rate, time-to-value, early adoption) rather than qualified revenue; I need to see whether the original record tracked anything downstream of activation, and whether the lift persisted beyond the first week. If memory_86 turns out to be a short-window proxy win with no revenue linkage, I would fall back to activation_messaging (memory_91) or reconsider. I am deliberately not verifying memory_57 or memory_44: referral incentives target established customers and enterprise sales-assist targets a segment that is not where the current decline is, so neither addresses this week's actual problem regardless of how well they verified. Running at standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout: the inherited evidence is suggestive but measures proxies, and the declines are recent enough that the underlying cause (competitor-driven mix shift versus genuine product friction) is not yet established. A standard experiment with revenue-quality instrumentation, not just completion rate, lets me distinguish those. Uncertainty preserved: I am treating the memory as generally reliable but not settled, and the intended action is contingent on what the two archive pulls return.
